title: Optimizing Multipliers: An Energy-Efficient Design Using a Novel 3:2 Compressor
problem: Power consumption and speed in multipliers depend critically on partial product addition efficiency. Existing 3:2 compressor designs derived from 4:2 compressors are suboptimal for multiplier applications.
motivation: Multipliers are fundamental arithmetic blocks in processors and accelerators. Improving compressor efficiency directly reduces multiplier power-delay product, benefiting data path design across computing systems.
method: Novel 3:2 compressor based on two-stage stacking concept to minimize circuit size while maintaining functionality. Applied to design 4-bit, 8-bit, and 16-bit multipliers.
key_novelty: Two-stage stacking compressor achieving 47.30% average power-delay product improvement over existing 3:2 compressor designs.
contributions: Novel 3:2 compressor architecture based on two-stage stacking
47.30% average improvement in power-delay product vs existing 3:2 compressors
Optimized for lower-bit multipliers (up to 16-32 bits)
limitations: Study limited to multipliers up to 16-32 bits; applicability to larger multipliers not addressed. Simulation results only; no silicon validation.
